Garden teaching case · Stage five

Enforcement Notice

No notice issued. The question was how water could move through a garden. The register establishes what the example describes. It supplies no observed injury, breached duty or body with standing to provide a remedy.

Disposition of the two findings

The yard location settles the location question for this example. The projection record advances no forecast on the strength of either report. The household discovery supplies no evidence of harm or responsibility. There is no supported remedy to demand, recipient to serve or referral to make on this evidence. Return to this puddle in the Atlas to follow another possible transfer.

Evidence reviewed

Entries 005 and 033 describe runoff reaching a stream. Entries 004, 008, 031 and 032 also connect the puddle to that stream underground. Entries 027 through 030 describe roof dew reaching garden soil through a barrel. The two open leads in the Temporal Projection Integrity Engine identify the observations needed to tell whether those transfers took place.

The first written snapshot and expanded written snapshot preserve the basis for that decision. Neither documents a damaged site, an affected person, a disputed action or an obligation to intervene. The absence of such a record leaves the condition of any real garden unknown.

What the reader can use

Someone who finds water at the stream can now trace two possible upstream histories and identify where observing the bank would help distinguish them. Someone checking a rain barrel can distinguish water collected overnight from water delivered through the hose. These are concrete uses of the map. This teaching record contains no report of a benefit received by an affected population.
